channel.title: AI GridWatch Blog
channel.description: Analysis and explainers on data center development, grid impact, and community advocacy.

item.title: The $327 Million Guess That Became $2.5 Billion: States Are Finally Learning What Data Center Tax Breaks Cost
item.description: Four states now lose more than $1 billion a year to data center sales-tax exemptions — and every one of them originally projected a fraction of that. Georgia revised its estimate up 664% in one January. Ohio's real cost came in at 12 times its projection. Indiana admitted 83% of its subsidy went to one company: Amazon. Fourteen states still won't publish a number at all. Here's what the June 2026 Good Jobs First report found, and what it means for the fiscal-note fight in your county.

item.title: Before You Approve a Data Center: 26 Questions Every Community Should Ask
item.description: A working synthesis of the checklists published by RFD-TV, Public Knowledge, EDF, the AI Now Institute, and the Alliance for the Great Lakes — collapsed into 26 questions, grouped by topic, with the reason each one matters and what a good answer looks like. Print it, bring it to the hearing, ask them all.

item.title: "Meta pays the full cost." Louisiana ratepayers pay $8–13 a month. Both are true.
item.description: Meta's Hyperion campus in rural Louisiana is now a 5-gigawatt, $50-billion-plus build — powered by ten new Entergy gas plants and a 60-mile transmission line whose $470M+ cost falls on ordinary customers. Meta says it pays the full cost of its electricity. State watchdogs say average Entergy Louisiana households will still pay $8–13 more per month. Both can be true. Here's how.

item.title: Five Auctions, $29 Billion: How Data Centers Took Over the PJM Capacity Market — and Sent Your Bill to the Moon
item.description: PJM's capacity auction price has gone from $29/MW-day to $325 in four years. Data centers drove 46% of the cost — $29.4 billion — across those auctions, and the grid's independent watchdog says ratepayers are footing the bill for power plants that may never be needed. Here's the full timeline, who pays, and the three reform proposals on the table right now.

item.title: One Project, Two Stories: How Data Center Developers Shop the Gaps Between Agencies
item.description: In Tucker County, West Virginia, one developer told the DEP it controlled 10,000 acres — and told the Department of Commerce its project was merely "conceptual." Both agencies say there's no contradiction, because neither one reviews the whole project. That gap isn't a West Virginia quirk. It's the buildout's default operating mode, and it shows up in seven recognizable forms — from "nonroad engine" turbine exemptions in Memphis to shell-company NDAs in Wisconsin to by-right zoning in Virginia. Here's the taxonomy, and the questions that close each gap.

item.title: DOE Just Named Data Centers the #1 Reason America Needs New Power Lines. Here's Why Your Community Should Read the Fine Print.
item.description: The Department of Energy's draft 2026 National Transmission Needs Study makes it official: load growth — led by data centers — is now the main reason the U.S. needs new transmission. Congestion already adds $11 billion a year to wholesale power costs, tens of billions in new lines are approved, and the study feeds directly into federal corridor designations that can override local siting authority. Public comments are open until September 7, 2026 — and the draft is full of numbers communities can use.

item.title: They Figured This Out Fifty Years Ago: What Oil, Wind, and Pipeline Towns Already Know About Protecting Neighbors
item.description: Property-value guarantees, voluntary buyouts, and community dividend funds aren't new ideas — they're battle-tested tools from decades of oil, wind, and pipeline fights. Data center communities are just the latest to need them, and the first to have the leverage to demand them all at once.

item.title: One in Five Electrons: BNEF Says Data Centers Will Consume 20% of U.S. Power by 2035
item.description: BloombergNEF just raised its U.S. data-center power forecast by 83% — to 194 GW by 2035 — meaning one out of every five units of electricity generated in the country would flow to a data center. With hyperscalers on track to spend $700 billion this year and 124 GW of on-site gas plants in the pipeline, the energy system your community depends on is being reshaped in real time.

item.title: Amazon Says It Picks Sites Where the Grid Needs Help. Here's What Communities Should Hear.
item.description: In a Latitude Media interview, Amazon's energy chief laid out a sophisticated site-selection strategy — picking locations where new load 'benefits the grid,' pledging full cost coverage, and touting a 52% water-efficiency gain. The claims are worth understanding, because the playbook is coming to a town near you.

item.title: A $15B Data Center Made Wisconsin Farmers Millionaires — and the Same Playbook Is Headed for 10 More Markets
item.description: In Port Washington, Vantage's $15B OpenAI–Oracle Stargate campus turned farmland into a lottery ticket — some sellers cleared millions, some wish they'd held out, and the neighbors who didn't sell face eminent domain. It's also a preview: the same power-first, low-opposition playbook is now spreading to 10 emerging markets, from Reno to Tulsa to New Mexico's $165B Stargate site.

item.title: Morgan Stanley Says Community Opposition Is the Biggest Threat to the Data Center Buildout. Are They Right?
item.description: Morgan Stanley warns that $156B in data center projects were canceled or delayed in 2025, with another $130B disrupted in Q1 2026 — driven by community resistance. We checked their thesis against our data.

item.title: New York Just Changed the Game: What EO 62 Means for Every Community Fighting a Data Center
item.description: Governor Hochul signed the nation's first statewide data center moratorium on July 14 — a 1-year pause on 50+ MW facilities that sets a precedent for community negotiating power nationwide.

item.title: Why Your Electric Bill Is Going Up — and What Data Centers Have to Do With It
item.description: Capacity charges, peak load auctions, and the coincident-peak trap: a plain-language guide to the parts of your electric bill you've never heard of — and why data center growth is making them explode.

item.title: How the Industry Files Your Protest: 'Social License' and the $64B Risk Column
item.description: Data-center developers don't have a risk category called 'protests.' They have 'social license to operate' — and organized community opposition has now blocked or delayed an estimated $64 billion in projects. Here's how the industry actually scores the risk that you'll show up to a hearing.

item.title: The Moratorium Wave: Why 14 States Are Pressing Pause on Data Centers
item.description: From Virginia's Loudoun County to rural Indiana, a rolling wave of moratorium bills and local zoning freezes is reshaping where the next generation of AI data centers can be built.

item.title: The Hidden Water Cost of Your AI Query: What the Data Actually Shows
item.description: A single ChatGPT query uses about 18 mL of water — roughly a medicine-cup pour. Multiply by billions of daily queries and the numbers start to matter, especially in water-stressed regions.

item.title: 233 GW of Demand Is Waiting in Line: Inside ERCOT's Data Center Queue
item.description: Texas's grid operator has 233 GW of large-load interconnection requests — roughly three times the state's current peak demand. Most of the queue is data centers. Here's what it means.
